claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old and lives with you.

Now I need to ask: **Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! And just to confirm: **Are you responsible for Alex's care, including providing for his needs such as food, clothes, and other expenses?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I take care of all his needs - his food, clothes, school things, everything he needs really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now I need to check a couple more things:

**Does Alex have any circumstances that might affect eligibility, such as:**
- Is he currently in hospital or care for an extended period?
- Does he work 24 hours or more per week?
- Does he receive any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually Alex has been in local authority care for a little while now - it's been a few months. But other than that, no - he doesn't work, and he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that important information. I need to understand this situation a bit better:

**When Alex is in local authority care, does he come home to stay with you for regular periods? For example, does he spend at least 24 hours a week at home, or does he come home for at least 2 nights in a row each week, or 7 days or more in a row?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure about the exact hours to be honest. Sometimes he does come home, but I couldn't tell you exactly how much time he spends here each week. It varies.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand, thank you for being honest about that. Let me ask one more question that might help:

**Do you regularly spend money on Alex - for example, on clothes, presents, food, pocket money, or contributing financially toward his care - even though he's in local authority care?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I still spend money on him - buying his clothes, getting him things he needs, that sort of thing.

## Summary

Based on the information you've provided, **I cannot make a definitive determination** about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

**Your situation:** Alex is 8 years old and normally would be eligible for Child Benefit. However, because he has been in local authority care for several months (more than 8 weeks), this affects the usual entitlement to Child Benefit.

**The complication:** There are exceptions that might allow you to continue receiving Child Benefit even when a child is in care, such as:
- If the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home, or
- If they spend 2 nights in a row each week or 7 days or more in a row at home

You've mentioned that Alex does come home sometimes and it varies, but you're not sure of the exact hours per week. You also mentioned you regularly spend money on him, which can be relevant.

**What you should do:** Because this is a complex situation with specific exceptions, I recommend you **contact HMRC's Child Benefit Office directly**. They can:
- Review the specific details of Alex's care arrangement
- Determine which exceptions might apply to your situation
- Give you a definitive answer about your eligibility

You can contact them by phone or through their online form to discuss your circumstances in detail.
